# Visual Algos

A **desktop app** that turns a computer-science topic into a
**3Blue1Brown-style [Manim](https://www.manim.community/) video** — generated by
AI and **rendered locally on your own machine**. Type a topic, Gemini writes the
Manim scene, and the app runs Manim to produce a real MP4 in your library.

No servers, no accounts, no cloud storage. The only thing that leaves your
machine is the topic text you send to the Gemini API.

```
┌───────────────────────── Electron app ─────────────────────────┐
│                                                                 │
│  Renderer (React UI)          Main process (Node)               │
│  ┌───────────────┐  IPC       ┌──────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ Library / New │ ─────────▶ │ createVisualization          │  │
│  │ Detail / Set. │           │   1. Gemini → Manim scene ────┼──┼─▶ Gemini API
│  │  (live status)│ ◀───────── │   2. static safety scan      │  │
│  └───────────────┘  changes   │   3. spawn `manim` → MP4 ─────┼──┼─▶ local python + Manim
│         ▲                     │   4. save to library.json     │  │
│         │ vizmedia://<id>     └──────────────────────────────┘  │
│         └───────────────── userData/videos/<id>.mp4             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## How it works

1. You add a **Gemini API key** in Settings (stored locally).
2. On `New`, you enter a topic. The main process asks **Gemini** for a
   self-contained Manim scene and runs a **static safety scan** on the code.
3. It writes the scene to a temp dir and runs **`manim`** (your local Python) to
   render an MP4, then copies it into the app's data folder.
4. The library and detail pages update **live** over IPC as the job moves through
   *Writing scene → Rendering → Ready*, then play the video.

Everything is stored locally:

- `userData/library.json` — your visualization metadata
- `userData/videos/<id>.mp4` — rendered videos
- `userData/settings.json` — API key, model, python path

(`userData` is the standard Electron per-user app data dir.)

## Requirements

- **Node.js 20+** (to build/run the app).
- A **Gemini API key** — free from [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey).
- To render, the app needs **Python 3.10+ with Manim** on your machine, plus
  Manim's system libraries:
  - **ffmpeg** (video encoding)
  - **cairo** and **pango** (Manim rendering)
  - a **LaTeX** install (only if you want mathematical formulas via `MathTex`)

The app **detects** these on startup and shows their status in **Settings**. If
Manim is missing it can create a managed Python virtualenv and `pip install
manim` for you — but the system libraries above still need your OS package
manager.

Install hints:

| OS      | Command                                                                 |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| macOS   | `brew install python ffmpeg cairo pango` then `pip3 install manim` (LaTeX: `brew install --cask mactex-no-gui`) |
| Ubuntu  | `sudo apt install python3 python3-pip ffmpeg libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev texlive` then `pip3 install manim` |
| Windows | Install Python + ffmpeg, then `pip install manim` (see Manim docs for MiKTeX) |

See the [Manim installation guide](https://docs.manim.community/en/stable/installation.html)
for details.

## Develop

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # launches the Electron app with hot reload
```

Then open **Settings**, paste your Gemini API key, confirm the render
environment is green, and create a video from **New**.

## Build a distributable

```bash
npm run build      # bundle main + preload + renderer (out/)
npm run package    # build an installer for your OS with electron-builder (dist/)
```

`electron-builder` targets: `.dmg`/`.zip` (macOS), `.nsis` (Windows),
`.AppImage` (Linux). See `electron-builder.yml`.

## Project layout

```
src/
  shared/types.ts        Shared types + IPC channel names (main ⇄ renderer)
  main/                  Electron main process
    index.ts             App lifecycle, window, vizmedia:// protocol
    ipc.ts               IPC handlers + change broadcast
    service.ts           create → Gemini → render pipeline
    gemini.ts            Gemini call
    manim.ts             Local Manim render via child_process
    manimPrompt.ts       Prompt, response schema, code safety scan
    env.ts               Detect python/manim/ffmpeg; managed venv installer
    store.ts             Local JSON store (settings + library)
    paths.ts             userData paths
  preload/index.ts       contextBridge → window.api
  renderer/              React UI (Vite + Tailwind + React Router)
    src/pages/           Library, New, Detail, Settings
    src/components/       Nav, cards, badges, code block
    src/lib/hooks.ts     Live data hooks over window.api
```

## Security notes

- **Context isolation is on**; the renderer has no Node access and talks to the
  main process only through the typed `window.api` bridge.
- The generated Python is **arbitrary code executed by Manim**. Mitigations:
  1. a **static denylist** rejects `os`, `subprocess`, `open`, `eval`, `exec`,
     sockets, etc. before rendering;
  2. it runs under **your own user account** and only ever writes to a temp dir
     and the app's videos folder.
  For stronger isolation you could render inside a container/sandbox — a good
  follow-up, out of scope for this MVP.
- Your Gemini API key is stored in plain JSON under `userData`. That's typical
  for local dev tools; a future version could use the OS keychain.
